ticket.title: Evaluate a shared process-execution crate: probe tool availability, run captured, extract first diagnostic
acceptance_criteria: ANALYSIS 2026-11-06 - and my recommendation is to NOT build this yet
with one exception.\n\nMeasured duplication: process spawning appears in outfeed (12 sites)
miter (4)
storypole (2)
joiner (2)
rabbet (1)

sawhorse (1) and common (1: gaugeblock-git). First-diagnostic extraction exists exactly once (outfeed gate/execute.rs::first_meaningful_line). So the repeated thing is not verification - it is probe/spawn/capture/classify/first-line

and gaugeblock-git is already the precedent for that living in common.\n\nWhy a shared VERIFICATION crate is wrong: the three tools answer different questions. storypole asks whether a task's configured gate passed and what receipt proves it; miter asks what the compilers say at AST-precise spans; outfeed asks whether each gate step passed and which line to show. Unifying the policy would force one shape on three questions

and the contract that matters (the receipt / SpoolEntry) already lives in gaugeblock-contracts.\n\nWhat WOULD justify a crate: tool availability probing plus captured execution plus first-diagnostic extraction

with >=2 consumers needing identical behaviour. Candidates are outfeed's cmd.rs and storypole's sh -c usage; miter produces structured diagnostics rather than text. Names considered: gaugeblock-process (recommended - says what it does); '-'development'/'coding' rejected as vague grab-bag names.\n\nBlocked on GB-269 being fixed first: if receipts record which command ran
the need for a shared runner becomes measurable rather than assumed.
